headline: Free Fruit for a Million: How Kansas City Built a National Orchard Movement
meta_description: The Giving Grove has planted 14,000 trees across 17 cities, turning vacant land into free community orchards that serve over a million people.
summary_short: A Kansas City nonprofit that started with one small orchard now runs 847 free fruit orchards across the country, proving that shared knowledge beats isolated effort.
body:
What began as a single stand of fruit trees on a shuttered schoolhouse corner in Kansas City's Waldo neighborhood thirteen years ago has grown into a national movement. The Giving Grove now tends 14,000 trees across 847 orchards in 17 cities, with more than a million people living within walking distance of free fruit they can harvest. At Kansas City Academy, students step outside during lunch to pick jujubes straight from the branches. For senior Nova Henry, it feels like stepping into a fairy tale. But the real magic lies not in the trees themselves, but in the ecosystem of knowledge that keeps them thriving.

The organization's secret is refusing to simply plant and disappear. Founder Kevin Birzer built the model on shared expertise from day one—training orchard stewards, offering pruning support, hosting workshops, and planning for succession when caretakers move on. About 1,700 stewards across the country maintain these relationships. At Kansas City Academy alone, science teacher Janet Porter finds that help is always a phone call away. The trees create a ripple effect too: they attract insects, which draw songbirds and predators like hawks. One student even turned pruning experience into a job at a tree nursery.

Kansas City, which now hosts 248 free orchards with nearly 4,600 fruit, nut, and berry trees, has become the template. Nine years ago, St. Louis asked for help. Now conversations are underway with San Francisco, Minneapolis, and New York City. Each community gets trees suited to its climate and growing conditions—no chemicals required. Running on just over $1 million annually, mostly from 1% for the Planet's corporate network, the Giving Grove only enters communities that invite it. Right now, it's working through a backlog of invitations. As marketing director Sarah Sikich notes, planting fruit trees is something nearly everyone can support.
quick_facts: 14,000 trees planted across 17 cities in 14 years
Kansas City has 248 free orchards with nearly 4,600 trees
1,700 orchard stewards maintain the network nationwide
Over 1 million people live within walking distance of an orchard
Funded by 1% for the Planet and individual donors
